item.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
item.description: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: SpaceX deploys Starlink satellites in Starship test, but booster crashes into Gulf
item.description: SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. It deployed several satellites for the Starlink constellation, but there was a problem with its booster.
item.content:encoded: SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. It deployed several satellites for the Starlink constellation, but there was a problem with its booster.

item.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
item.description: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
item.description: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.

item.title: This week in science: PTSD prediction, phishing while tired, an exoplanet
item.description: The regular news roundup with NPR's science podcast Short Wave covers a possible use for AI in emergency rooms, a distant planet and the link between cybersecurity and Daylight Saving Time.

item.title: Scientists think they've found ancient remnants of dinosaur blood
item.description: Scientists have studied plenty of dinosaur bones, eggs and footprints. Now, some think they've found their strongest evidence yet of dinosaur blood.
item.content:encoded: Scientists have studied plenty of dinosaur bones, eggs and footprints. Now, some think they've found their strongest evidence yet of dinosaur blood.

item.title: Mice can learn to fight by watching tiny rodent cage matches, study finds
item.description: Brain scientists set up "gladiator style" cage matches for mice — and found that simply observing fighting matches can rewire a mouse's brain to resemble those who actually fought.
